S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.

subtypes.Self-Blame: Blaming oneself for the occurrence of the trauma or for not preventing it.
subtypes.Blaming Others: Distorting the situation to blame specific others for the occurrence or damage of the trauma.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

symptom.disease_info: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder is a trauma- and stressor-related disorder that develops after exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, with persistent intrusion symptoms, avoidance, negative alterations in cognition or mood, and heightened arousal lasting more than one month and causing impairment. Its course may be delayed, chronic, or fluctuate with reminders, and it is distinguished from acute stress disorder by duration and from adjustment disorder by the required traumatic exposure and characteristic trauma-linked symptom clusters.

patient.stressor: Peter and his wife took in her brother during a family dispute, and the household tension culminated in a frightening workshop confrontation in which Peter was threatened with a heavy tool and believed he might be seriously injured. At first he tried to fold the episode into one of his usual stories, but over 2 years and 4 months his sleep became unreliable, unwanted memories intruded, he avoided the workshop and family gatherings involving that relative, and he found he could not remember a key part of how the confrontation ended. His view of family trust narrowed, he blamed himself for letting the arrangement continue, and his irritability and watchfulness made volunteering and painting less steady, though he continued some routines with support from his wife. He sought psychiatric care himself after a senior-center talk on trauma made him recognize that the problem had become more than ordinary family stress.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I can get to bed, but I lie there listening for noises in the house or I wake up from a bad dream about the workshop and then I'm wide awake for an hour or two.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: Out of nowhere I'll see his hand with that heavy tool again, like a picture that pops into my head while I'm shaving or working on a painting, and it still makes my chest tighten.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I came in because I keep steering clear of my own workshop and any family get-together where my brother-in-law might be, and after all this time I'm tired of planning my life around not running into those reminders.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: I remember the shouting and the tool plain enough, but there's a blank spot right around how it actually ended, like somebody cut a few minutes out of the story.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.
S072.manifestation: I used to think family was where you could let your guard down, but now I catch myself thinking you can't really trust people, even the ones who sit at your own table.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.
S073.manifestation: I keep telling myself I should have put my foot down sooner and never let him stay with us, because maybe none of this would have happened if I'd handled it like a man.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: I'm not throwing things or anything, but I snap at my wife over little stuff, like where she put my paint brushes or if she asks me twice about supper plans.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.
S079.manifestation: Even at the senior center or church basement, I find myself checking who came in, where the door is, and whether anyone is standing too close behind me.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I still manage the basics, but I’ve stopped doing regular volunteer jobs that involve the workshop or big family events, and my painting comes in fits and starts because I avoid the place where I kept most of my supplies.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on since that confrontation with my brother-in-law about two years and four months ago.
